report.clinical_summary: Patient diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) a few months ago, currently on watch-and-wait with monthly blood tests. Symptoms include fatigue (6 months, gradually worsening), night sweats, swollen lymph nodes in neck, and unexplained weight loss (5 pounds). Fatigue is the primary concern, impacting daily life. No treatment started due to stable white blood cell count. Patient trusts doctor's judgment and follows recommendations.

making it harder to get through my day without feeling drained
it's impacting my daily life quite significantly

consequences.reasoning: Patient describes fatigue as draining and reports it makes daily activities harder, with explicit statement that it impacts daily life significantly. They have adjusted sleep schedule and take breaks, indicating moderate impact on functioning.
